questions.stem: Regulators will audit an approval chain whose steps never change. Which style does the first page match to that need?

options.text: Graph-based, with nodes and edges drawn beforehand
options.says: The first page says to use the graph style "when the process is known and must be auditable: an approval chain, an order flow".

options.text: Model-driven, with the model choosing at each turn
options.says: Ruled out because the table gives the next step to "The model, at each turn", and "The route is whatever the model chooses".

options.text: Typed, with each reply validated against a schema
options.says: Ruled out because "Types guard the edges of the model's freedom. They do not choose the route."

options.text: A mix in which the model picks the route and a graph logs it
options.says: Ruled out because "The model fills in a node. It does not pick the route."

questions.stem: A team wants to be able to replace its agent framework later. Which design choice keeps that cheap?

options.text: Copying the framework's source into the product's repository
options.says: Ruled out because the trap is "Coupling the whole codebase to one framework", and a copy of the source ties the repository to one.

options.text: Storing the sessions in the format that the framework defines
options.says: Ruled out because "Your state format, your tool definitions and your tests then follow the framework's releases."

options.text: Wrapping each model call and tool in a function of its own
options.says: The page says "Keeping the model call behind a thin function of your own limits the damage".

options.text: Importing the framework's types directly in each module
options.says: Ruled out because the aim is "so that a change of framework is a change in one place", and imports in each module spread the change.
